_meta.scope: Whole-cast relationship graph for Alice's Adventures in Wonderland as a realistic 1862 dream drama. Nodes are CHAR-* ids from bible/characters/index.json; CRE-* appears only for CRE-001, the real silent white rabbit of the waking frame (bible/creatures/index.json). Every edge carries a controlled type, strength 1-5, direction, and a state sequence anchored to story/events.json event ids and chapters.
inputs: bible/cultivation.json SUP-001, SUP-002, SUP-005, SUP-012, SUP-014
_meta.frame_rule: Every dream-layer edge (ev0002-ev0052) exists only inside Alice's dream (SUP-001) and ends when she wakes at ev0053 (ch012#p64). Only CHAR-alice, CHAR-alice-sister, CHAR-family-housemaid and CRE-001 have waking-layer relationships.

type_enum.household: belongs to / is kept by the same household without a service contract (e.g. the Duchess's cat)
type_enum.master_servant: employer or sovereign over a servant, page, herald, footman, soldier or officer (directed: master -> servant)
type_enum.authority_subject: an adult or office-holder exercising power over someone not in their service: judge/defendant, monarch/guest, examiner/child, gatekeeper/visitor (directed: authority -> subject)
type_enum.mentor_pupil: teacher or examiner who instructs (directed: mentor -> pupil)
type_enum.guide: leads, lures or escorts the other through the story (directed: guide -> guided)
type_enum.companionship: peers sharing a group, table or journey
type_enum.alliance: one side protects or sides with the other
type_enum.affection: warmth or friendship offered across the pair
type_enum.rivalry: peer squabbling or blame without real threat
type_enum.dream_echo: H1 ruling 5.3 B / SUP-002 doubling: a waking-world person or animal reappears transformed in Alice's dream (directed: waking source -> dream side)

strength_scale.2: minor: one scene with some consequence
strength_scale.3: notable: recurring or shapes a sequence
strength_scale.4: major: shapes an act of the film
strength_scale.5: defining: drives the main line and the climax

_meta.key_rule: key: true marks edges that drive the main line (Alice's identity and her stand against nonsensical adult authority, closing in the trial and the waking return). QA samples these against the source.
_meta.state_rule: states[] is chronological; from_chapter is the source chapter number of event_id (events.json). A state holds until the next one. inferred: true on a state marks a designed staging beat with its reason.
_meta.secret_rule: secret.hidden_from lists characters who never know; audience knowledge and the reveal point are given in reveal_chapter/reveal_event, or never_revealed: true. Screenplay must not state a never_revealed fact in dialogue.
_meta.edge_key: An edge is identified by (from, to, type); no pair carries the same type twice. No edge-ID prefix is registered in WRITE_RULES.md section 4, so none is minted.
